headline: Structured representations and pruning replace dense computation in sequence analysis
label: Scalable Sequence Analysis Algorithms
summary: Recent preprints report linear-time, multithreaded, and pangenome-scale methods that trade dense computation for pruned or structured alternatives.
synthesis: The dominant thread in this set is reducing the cost of sequence-derived computation by changing the underlying representation or algorithm. LinearRaccess replaces span-limited RNA folding with beam-pruned inside-outside dynamic programming, giving deterministic O(N) accessibility estimates without base-pair span limits. Hub labeling substitutes exact distance queries for dense all-pairs snarl distance matrices in the vg distance index, enabling this on large human pangenome graphs. Zindex combines interleaved ZOR filters, color-preserving merging, and SIMD acceleration for compact colored sequence search across millions of sequences. On the single-cell side, brisc targets reproducible multithreaded CPU analysis, and the extended simpleaf reports lower runtime and memory than cyto and Cell Ranger for sub-gene probe-based quantification. The new element is that efficiency gains are reported alongside exactness or accuracy claims, although the problems addressed differ across items.
